A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAT architecture and research program. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, pseudocode, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original pretraining, latency, downstream evaluation, supervised fine-tuning, ablation, and retrieval results, including experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds architectural comparisons and larger-model throughput measurements. It distinguishes baseline results borrowed from another study.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(3) and Listings 1–2 retain the same recurrence, chunk attention, gates, positional encoding, and training/inference procedures. The RAT-SWA hybrid is also retained. FLASH and dilated attention are additional comparators, not changes to RAT.

E1.justification: V2 adds BoolQ but removes the LongBench few-shot category comprising TREC, TriviaQA, and SAMSum. It also removes the passage-only NarrativeQA3 evaluation from v1 Appendix C.3, eliminating a distinct QA setting. The eight documented RULER tasks are retained and relocated, despite v2's unsupported claim of nine.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 3–4 substantially expand the corresponding comparisons with cited Mamba-family, DeltaNet, and GatedDeltaNet results, including GatedDeltaNet-SWA. V1 explicitly excluded GatedDeltaNet from its tables. V2 Appendix C.1 additionally evaluates FLASH and RNN-Dilated attention against RAT.

E3.justification: V2 extends throughput benchmarking to 7B and 13B models, adds raw alongside normalized commonsense accuracy and memory-slot accounting, and introduces FLOPs-matched architectural comparisons. V1's dedicated 16K accuracy evaluation is no longer presented, although its training setup remains documented. The retained 4K pretraining, SFT, and RULER procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds targeted analyses comparing RAT's hierarchical chunk organization with FLASH's additive organization and its global access with sliding dilated attention. Existing parameter-allocation, positional-encoding, reversed-design, and RoPE/NoPE extrapolation analyses remain. Moving RULER results into the main text adds no new retrieval analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Input-length percentile summaries retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds BoolQ, raw-accuracy and external-baseline scores, FLASH perplexity of 14.4 versus RAT's retained 13.34, and new larger-model throughput results. Few-shot and 16K accuracy entries are removed; matched retained 4K and RULER scores are unchanged. Revised CSR averages are not same-setting gains. V2 also inconsistently reports 1.3B attention throughput as 3052 in Table 1 and 3152 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The recurrence and attention equations, chunk definitions, parameter-budget reasoning, and asymptotic mixing complexity remain unchanged. V2 adds resource accounting and explanatory discussion, but no new formal derivation, theorem, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The central RAT interpolation claim, hybrid benefits, and headline training/generation speedups remain. V2 makes scalability and compatibility with multidimensional parallelism an explicit contribution, whereas v1 discusses compatibility tentatively in Section 2.4. This is a limited strengthening of the claimed contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving FLASH's output-scale conflicts and dilated attention's limited global perception. It removes v1's qualification that concatenated short documents may not teach true long-context capabilities and its suggestion to enlarge local windows for the 16K setting. The principal model-scale and length-generalization limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the added comparator configurations, including dilation rate 64 with dilated attention in half the layers, and explains how heads and chunks could be distributed across GPUs. Existing RAT pseudocode, principal hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: Related work shifts substantially toward fixed-memory limitations, hierarchical versus hybrid architectures, and distinctions from FLASH and dilated attention. V2 adds positioning against log-linear attention and gated slot attention, among other references, while removing several historical RNN discussions. It also reverses v1's decision to exclude contemporary recurrent baselines from tabulated comparisons.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative, experimental discussion, and related work are extensively rewritten. Architecture and scalable implementation become separate sections, experiments are regrouped, retrieval results enter the main narrative, the 16K accuracy subsection disappears, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: V2 combines the architecture illustrations, removes the main latency figure's prefilling panel while retaining its appendix data, and adds throughput and architectural-comparison tables. Evaluation tables gain memory-slot columns and revised task/metric structures. The retrieval table moves into the main text, and the 16K accuracy table is removed.

improvement.justification: V2's broader baseline comparisons, FLOPs-matched controls, and clearer architectural explanation improve assessability. However, it removes few-shot and 16K accuracy evidence, including the hybrid's 22.6 versus attention's 23.3 F1 on passage-only NarrativeQA, together with relevant qualifications. New retrieval-task-count and throughput inconsistencies further weaken reporting reliability. These gains and losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
